## Raw-data manifest

Every confirmatory number in this paper comes from simulated data, generated by `rt/sim.py` from the seeds listed below; no external data enter H1 to H3. Two small derived files in `data/` feed the descriptive overlay and the illustrative survey comparison. They are in the repository, with their provenance in `data/PROVENANCE.md`.

```{=latex}
\begingroup\scriptsize\raggedright\setstretch{1}
```

## Run ledgers

Each run appends one row to a ledger when it finishes: `results/ledger.csv` for the laptop and one `results/cloud/ledger*.csv` per rented instance. The 96 rows below are every row of every ledger, in order of start time; all have return code 0. Seconds are wall-clock seconds of the run that finished, training and evaluation together; a resumed run records only its last segment, and runs shared the hardware, so the seconds do not sum to instance time.

## Cost record

| item | amount |
|-------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| sweep instance 1 | about \$2.11 |
| sweep instance 2 | about \$4.29 |
| sweep instance 3 | about \$4.60 |
| sweep instance 4 | about \$3.35 |
| total, four sweep instances | about \$14.35 |
| pilot instance (about 99 minutes), if billed separately | about \$0.71 |
| total, range | \$14.35 to about \$15.06 |
| instance-hours | about 41 |
| price | \$0.35 per GPU-hour (RTX A6000) |
| set aside for the sweep | \$12 |
| pre-registered cloud cap (PREREG section 10) | \$15 of a \$20 credit |
| owner's overall hard limit | \$20 |
| laptop runs | no rented compute |

: Cost record: estimated cloud spend by instance, the total as a range, and the budget limits it is read against (from `docs/DECISIONS.md`). {#tbl-cost}


The spend is estimated from instance time at the listed price and has not yet been reconciled against the provider's bill, which the command line does not expose. The decisions log gives the total as "about \$14.35 over four instances" with the pilot included; the first instance's figure was read from the provider's console, and it is not known whether it includes the separate pilot instance (about \$0.71). The total is therefore between \$14.35 and about \$15.06: over the \$12 set aside for the sweep, and at or just over the \$15 pre-registered cloud cap depending on the pilot. The entry in [Appendix @sec-app-deviations] gives the cause of the overrun (a stalled file copy).

| laptop | Apple-silicon Mac (M2 Pro), PyTorch `mps` device; sizes xs and s, the gate, every benchmark cache and all analysis |
| cloud | one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB) per instance, Thunder Compute, 8 vCPUs, CUDA; sizes m and l and Family B; TF32 matrix multiplies and one CPU thread per process, set by environment variables (`TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=1`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`) |
| paper | Quarto with XeLaTeX; TeX Gyre Pagella |

: Software and hardware {#tbl-environment}


Training is seeded per step, so a run follows the same data stream on any machine; numbers agree to floating-point tolerance, not bit for bit. Laptop cells reproduce to 1e-6. Cloud cells used TF32, and re-evaluating two of them in full precision moved excess error by up to 0.04 points and the gap by up to 0.0002 (`docs/DECISIONS.md`).

## Commands

The repository has no Makefile; every step is one command, run with `uv` from the repository root.

| command | what it does |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `uv sync` | create the locked environment |
| `uv run pytest` | the test suite |
| `uv run python -m rt.gate` | benchmark, planted-value and learning checks; writes `results/gate.json` with the code hash |
| `uv run python -m rt.sweep` | train and evaluate the grid (refuses without a green gate at the current hash); see `cloud/README.md` and `scripts/mac_sweep.sh` |
| `uv run python -m rt.train`, `-m rt.evaluate` | one run: train a cell; evaluate its checkpoints into `results/metrics/` |
| `uv run python -m analysis.report` | `RESULTS.md`, `results/summary.csv`, `results/hypotheses.json` and the report figures, from `results/metrics/` |
| `uv run python -m analysis.paper_build` | every generated file of this paper: variables, tables, figures and appendix sections |
| `quarto render docs/paper` | this PDF (and its `.tex` source) |
| `uv run pytest -q tests/test_paper_build.py` | checks that every variable resolves, that the decisions match `results/hypotheses.json` and that the generated tables reproduce `results/summary.csv` |

: Commands {#tbl-commands}


`analysis.report` reads `results/metrics/`, which is in the repository, so every verdict can be recomputed without training anything. Model checkpoints (about 6 GB) and the benchmark cache (about 9 GB) are not in the repository; the cache is rebuilt by `rt.evaluate`.

## Seed scheme

```{=latex}
\begingroup\scriptsize\raggedright\setstretch{1}
```

| what | generator | note |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| training batch at step k of a run with seed s | `SeedSequence([s, 0xA11CE, k])` (NumPy) | depends only on the seed and the step: every cell of a family at a given seed sees the same paths (and, for windowed cells, the same origins); a resumed run follows the same stream |
| parameter initialisation | `torch.manual_seed(s)` | s ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} |
| evaluation set i of a family (i = 0..5 for ρ = 0, 0.2, …, 1; i = 6 for the prior set) | `SeedSequence([10000 + i, tag])`, tag `0xE0A` (Family A) or `0xE0B` (Family B) | a stream separate from every training stream; the same sets for every run |
| survey drop-rule range | seed `(30000, 0x5BF)` | 100,000 simulated Family B paths (`docs/DECISIONS.md`) |
